issues.legal_issue: The statutory protection for a sick industrial company extends to a bank-debt recovery application that may lead to execution or distress against the company’s property, and that protection prevails over the recovery procedure in the event of conflict.
material_facts: A financial institution obtained a recovery order against the company and pursued recovery through a tribunal and sale of the company’s property, which had been mortgaged as security.
The company invoked the industrial-company rehabilitation process while the recovery and sale dispute was ongoing.
The recovery statute gives its provisions an overriding effect but also provides that it is in addition to, and not in derogation of, the industrial-company statute.
issues.conclusion: The industrial-company statute prevails in this conflict, and its protection covers a recovery application that results in, or may result in, execution or distress against the sick company’s property. The High Court’s order was nevertheless set aside and the company’s writ petitions were dismissed because the recovery proceedings had been concluded.
issues.legal_principle: The court construed Section 22 of the Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act, 1985, in context and held that it bars recovery proceedings under the Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993, where the statutory rehabilitation process is active and the proceedings would lead to execution or distress against the company’s property. Section 34(1) of the recovery statute gives it overriding effect, but Section 34(2) preserves the industrial-company statute; the latter provision prevents the recovery statute from derogating from the rehabilitation process. The court applied the principles of purposive and harmonious construction discussed in Ram Narain v. Simla Banking & Industrial Co. Ltd., LIC v. D.J. Bahadur, Maharashtra Tubes Ltd. v. State Industrial & Investment Corpn. of Maharashtra Ltd., Allahabad Bank v. Canara Bank, and Reserve Bank of India v. Peerless General Finance and Investment Co. Ltd. It distinguished Kailash Nath Agarwal v. Pradeshiya Industrial & Investment Corporation of U.P. Ltd., which concerned protection for guarantors rather than the scope of protection for the sick company itself.

rule.if: secured_debt_recovery_proceeding and rehabilitation_process_active and recovery_targets_company_property and not rehabilitation_authority_consent

predicates.secured_debt_recovery_proceeding: A bank or financial institution pursued a tribunal-based proceeding to recover a debt from a borrower.
predicates.rehabilitation_process_active: An inquiry, scheme process, implementation process, or appeal concerning the company's rehabilitation was active.
predicates.recovery_targets_company_property: The recovery proceeding could result in execution or distress against property of the industrial company.
predicates.rehabilitation_authority_consent: The rehabilitation authority consented to the recovery proceeding continuing.

issues.definition: When a debt-recovery proceeding may reach a company's property while its rehabilitation process is active and the rehabilitation authority has not consented, the recovery proceeding is stayed.

issues.legal_issue: A company cannot obtain relief under the statutory stay to undo recovery proceedings that the court finds were already concluded before the company sought that protection.
material_facts: The recovery order was made before the company invoked the rehabilitation process.
The company’s property was auctioned and the successful purchaser deposited the sale price before the company invoked that process.
The company later challenged the recovery and sale through writ petitions.
issues.conclusion: The company was not entitled to relief in its writ petitions because the recovery proceedings had been concluded; the petitions were dismissed and the appeal was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: The stay in Section 22 of the Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act, 1985, operates against proceedings that are pending or are to be proceeded with; it does not provide relief to undo recovery proceedings that have already been concluded. The court relied on its finding that the recovery proceedings had concluded and the sale price had been deposited before the company invoked the statutory protection.

predicates.writ_challenge_to_recovery_action: A company brought a writ proceeding seeking to set aside recovery action against it.
predicates.recovery_proceeding_concluded_before_pro: The court found that the recovery proceeding had concluded before the company sought statutory protection.

issues.definition: A company bringing a writ challenge to recovery action receives no relief under the statutory stay when the recovery proceeding had already concluded before it sought protection.
